purpose: THE C++ APPLICABLE SET, machine-readable: one row per relationship type the C++ language can express (decided from the PINNED GRAMMAR's own enumeration, never from the ten-value matrix), with the emission site in src/ast/real-cpp-analyzer.ts and at least one fixture that can go RED for it (measured by the real fixture runner with the emission removed) — plus the ruled non-applicable canonical values, the C++ construct surface, and the C++-specific rulings the D1 handoff asked to be proved rather than assumed.

grammar.enumeration: the pinned wasm enumerated through web-tree-sitter's Language API (nodeTypeCount / nodeTypeIsNamed / nodeTypeForId). ERROR and MISSING are universal parser outputs, not grammar productions, and are classified separately in cpp-completeness.json.

admissibilityRule: APPLICABLE iff every construct production the value needs exists in the pinned grammar's own enumeration AND the analyzer has an emission site AND at least one fixture carries a positive expectation row AND that fixture goes RED when the emission is removed. A value failing any conjunct is a finding, not a note.

decorates.reason: no decorator/annotation production exists in the pinned C++ grammar. It DOES have attribute_specifier / attribute_declaration / __attribute__ (GNU and C++11 attributes), adjudicated here rather than ignored: an attribute names no callable declaration of its own (it is a keyword/macro-written specifier), and the analyzer records export attributes as the `exports` edge + symbol metadata — the same ruling the java lane applied to annotations (references+isAnnotation; decorates reserved for runtime callable decorators). No cpp fixture expects a `decorates` row and the analyzer emits none.
decorates.vocabularyRuling: extended value, NOT APPLICABLE to C++.

renders.reason: no JSX/element-construction production exists in the pinned C++ grammar; C++ never creates a component-element pair.
renders.vocabularyRuling: extended value (TSX/JSX), NOT APPLICABLE to C++.

mixes_in.reason: no mixin/with production exists in the pinned C++ grammar. Multiple inheritance expresses composition of base classes and is carried by `extends`; there is no separate mixin application construct to publish.
mixes_in.vocabularyRuling: extended value (Dart `with`), NOT APPLICABLE to C++.

part_of.reason: C++'s file-inclusion construct is `#include`, which IS a module edge and is published as `imports`; there is no part-file directive that shares one scope without importing (the construct `part_of` exists to distinguish).
part_of.vocabularyRuling: extended value (Dart `part`/`part of`), NOT APPLICABLE to C++.

classes / structs / unions.ruling: a class is a symbol; its members are contains, its bases extends + implements, its virtual overrides are overrides, its constructions instantiates.

templates (declaration + type arguments).ruling: a template ARGUMENT is a type mention (references); `new X<T>` strips the arguments and instantiates X. A template DECLARATION is a declaration form, not a relationship kind: its members are contained by the enclosing class/namespace, and its parameters are not symbols. `template_instantiation` is a compile-time specialization and is NOT the `instantiates` value (see rulings): measured 2026-10-18, `Box<int> b;` with `template <typename T> struct Box` emits the class's contains edges and NO instantiates edge — a template variable is not object creation.

namespaces.ruling: namespace -> member is contains; a qualified mention of a namespace-scoped name is references. Namespaces are NOT imports (imports is #include only) and NOT exports (no marker).

namespace alias / using-declaration / us.ruling: a using-dependency is published as references (the dependency edge the early residual analysis called the 'using half' of the old single imports bucket). A namespace ALIAS names a namespace, which is not a published declaration, so it emits no edge — measured in the census.

multiple inheritance.ruling: one base_class_clause holds a LIST of bases (base_class_clause_repeat1), so N bases = N extends edges and (for pure-virtual bases) N implements edges. It is not a distinct relationship type.

virtual / override / pure-virtual method.ruling: a derived method overriding a base virtual is overrides; a base that DECLARES a pure virtual is a contract and implementing it is implements. The `override`/`final` keyword is recorded as an evidence class, never invented when absent.

operator overloads.ruling: an operator overload is a declared member (symbol) named `operator+` etc.; it is contained by its class (`contains`), and a call-shaped use of it can be a calls/uses edge. Measured 2026-10-18 on the operator-EXPRESSION shape: `a + b` with `V operator+` declared in-file emits NO calls edge (the analyzer's own callee rule excludes operator-spelled targets from `calls`, a documented decision), so the expression form is a measured silence while the symbol and its containment are emitted. There is no `overloads` relationship value: overload relations are not a canonical kind, and the symbol's kind/name carries the fact.

lambda expressions (captures).ruling: a capture of a FILE-DECLARED name is a READ of that name and is emitted as `uses` from the enclosing function; a call INSIDE the lambda body is a `calls` edge from the enclosing function (measured 2026-10-18: `[g]() { return g; }` → uses work→g; `[](int x){ helper(x); }` → calls work→helper). A capture of a PARAMETER or local whose declaration is not published as a symbol emits no edge (parameters/locals are not symbols in this lane), and a capture with an initializer (`[b=a]`) emits no capture-list edge of its own. A lambda expression publishes no symbol, so no contains edge is fabricated for it.

structured bindings.ruling: a structured binding DECLARES local names (not published symbols) and READS the initializer's object: measured 2026-10-18, `P p; auto [a, b] = p;` emits `uses work→p` (the read) and NO uses edge for a/b (declaration positions). A local/parameter initializer name that is not a published symbol is a measured silence, not a fabricated edge.

concepts / requires (C++20).ruling: RULED: grammar-present but carrying NO relationship in this lane's model. A concept is a named constraint entity this analyzer does not publish as a symbol (publishing it would be a new symbol kind, not a relationship), and a requires_clause is a compile-time constraint, not a call/read/inheritance fact. Measured population is carried by the D2 census so this is a count, not a silence; if a future wave publishes concepts, `references` to the concept is the value they would carry.

friend declarations/definitions.ruling: a friend DEFINITION is a free function owned by no class (fixtures friend-definition-published / friend-owner-name-recovery pin this); a friend DECLARATION grants access and publishes no edge of its own.

preprocessor (#include / #define / condi.ruling: includes are imports; an export MARKER macro applied to a declaration is exports (the marker spelling decides); mutually exclusive conditional definitions are the ADAPTED `overrides` semantics used by the C lane as well (shape carried in metadata).

rulings.question: `implements`: is the canonical value applicable to C++?
rulings.measured: the pinned grammar has NO implements-clause production (implements_clause / class_interface_clause / super_interfaces all ABSENT — section 2 proves it). It DOES have class_specifier + base_class_clause + pure_virtual_clause; the analyzer emits implements at a measured site from (derived, pure-virtual base) pairs and the corpus carries them.
rulings.verdict: APPLICABLE BY ADAPTED SEMANTICS — a pure-virtual base is a contract. Ruling it non-applicable would contradict the emission and the fixtures; the adapted reading is declared in the value's rule and in script/m14/spec/cpp-completeness.json.
rulings.wholePopulation: implements 375 edges in 73 files across 8 repos (D2 census, 7,435 admitted files); payload split by pureVirtualCount in wholePopulationArms.census.implementsPayload

rulings.question: template_instantiation vs `instantiates`: the same word, the same value?
rulings.measured: `template_instantiation` (a compile-time type specialization, e.g. `Box<int>`) and `new_expression` (runtime object creation) are DIFFERENT productions. The `instantiates` value is emitted from new_expression only; a new of a template type strips `<>` and instantiates the base type name. No value is named after template instantiation, and no constructor-of-template edge is fabricated.
rulings.verdict: DISTINCT — a C++ template instantiation carries no relationship; `instantiates` = object creation. Recorded so no future reader derives the value from the wrong node.
rulings.wholePopulation: instantiates 3093 edges / template_instantiation 267 construct sites — different populations, as ruled

rulings.question: Are `using` / namespace declarations `imports`?
rulings.measured: `imports` is emitted from preproc_include only (site read from source). using_declaration is emitted as a references dependency (the using-half of the early residual analysis) and namespace containment as contains.
rulings.verdict: NO — `imports` is a module-path edge (#include); a using-dependency is a symbol/type dependency (references). The census counts both separately so the mapping is a number.

rulings.question: Does multiple inheritance need its own value?
rulings.measured: base_class_clause's shape is a repeated list of base_class items; the analyzer iterates it and emits one extends (and, where pure virtual, one implements) per base.
rulings.verdict: NO — multiple inheritance is N extends edges; the value set already expresses it, and the fixture pins a two-base class.
rulings.wholePopulation: extends 4331 edges; 114 classes with more than one base in 58 files / 5 repos
